executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports spanning October 2025 through May 2026 from ECDC and PAHO reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across Europe and the Americas. The Americas region faces particular pressure from vector-borne diseases including dengue and chikungunya, ongoing mpox transmission, and the persistent threat of avian influenza A(H5N1) with zoonotic spillover risk. Respiratory disease threats including seasonal influenza, RSV, and pertussis are showing resurgent activity in both hemispheres, with the Southern Hemisphere entering its 2026 respiratory season. Yellow fever activity and measles outbreaks indicate gaps in vaccination coverage that require urgent remediation.
bottomLine: The Americas and Europe face a complex multi-pathogen threat landscape dominated by dengue, avian influenza A(H5N1), mpox, pertussis resurgence, and the onset of Southern Hemisphere respiratory virus season requiring coordinated surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Dual PAHO updates (November 2025 and March 2026) indicating sustained and evolving transmission in animal reservoirs
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans with continued animal-sector exposure across the Americas
Repeated epidemiological updates suggest expanding geographic footprint and species range
threats.action: Enhance zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interface, enforce biosafety at poultry and dairy operations, accelerate pre-pandemic H5N1 vaccine stockpiling, and trigger incident management protocols for any confirmed human cases

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating elevated case counts
Historical context of record-breaking dengue seasons in Latin America in preceding years suggesting hyperendemicity
Multiple serotype co-circulation increases risk of severe dengue
threats.action: Activate vector control programs, strengthen hospital surge capacity for severe dengue case management, expand seroprevalence monitoring across endemic zones, and issue public health advisories for travellers

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission
Sustained circulation in the Americas following global emergency declarations
Risk of clade Ib introduction from affected African regions cannot be excluded
threats.action: Reinforce contact tracing and ring vaccination strategies, expand access to JYNNEOS vaccine, enhance laboratory diagnostics for clade differentiation, and strengthen surveillance at ports of entry

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicate persistent and potentially resurgent transmission
Dual alerts within a three-month window suggest waning population immunity and possible vaccine coverage gaps
Infants and unvaccinated adolescents at highest risk
threats.action: Audit national vaccination coverage rates, implement catch-up immunization campaigns, strengthen sentinel surveillance for infant hospitalizations, and reinforce Tdap recommendations for pregnant women and healthcare workers

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert January 2026 flagged simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation stressing healthcare systems
PAHO April 2026 alert marks start of Southern Hemisphere 2026 respiratory season
ECDC weekly threat reports spanning Weeks 16-20 of 2026 indicate ongoing European respiratory threat monitoring
Dual-pathogen pressure increases ICU and pediatric ward burden
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination for priority groups ahead of Southern Hemisphere season, ensure RSV monoclonal antibody availability for high-risk infants, activate hospital surge planning, and monitor antiviral resistance patterns

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026 indicating active transmission or elevated risk
Sylvatic yellow fever activity suggests epizootic spillover risk into unvaccinated human populations
Gaps in vaccination coverage in border and forest-fringe communities
threats.action: Accelerate reactive vaccination campaigns in at-risk municipalities, enforce international travel vaccination certificate requirements, strengthen epizootics surveillance in non-human primates, and preposition vaccine supplies

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 3 February 2026 signaling active cases or importation risk
Measles resurgence globally provides importation pressure into sub-optimally vaccinated communities
Any confirmed case in a region previously declared free constitutes a public health emergency
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments, implement outbreak response immunization in affected areas, strengthen case-based surveillance and laboratory confirmation, and issue alerts to healthcare providers for early detection

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 10 February 2026 indicating elevated transmission risk or active outbreak
Aedes vector populations expanded by climate patterns facilitate year-round transmission in tropical zones
Potential for geographic spread into previously unaffected temperate areas
threats.action: Enhance entomological surveillance, implement integrated vector management, monitor for neurological complications in reported cases, and coordinate with dengue response programs given shared vector

amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific reports identified in this dataset; however, pertussis resurgence may partly reflect atypical Bordetella pertussis strains with altered vaccine antigen profiles requiring macrolide susceptibility monitoring
Influenza antiviral resistance monitoring warranted given dual-season A/B co-circulation flagged in PAHO and ECDC reports
Dengue clinical management protocols should be reviewed given risk of empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic use driving secondary AMR in co-infected patients
emergingPatterns: Temporal clustering of dual PAHO H5N1 alerts (November 2025 and March 2026) suggests progressive geographic and host-range expansion of H5N1 in the Western Hemisphere
Two pertussis alerts within 90 days (December 2025 and March 2026) signal a multi-wave resurgence pattern consistent with waning immunity in adolescent and adult cohorts
Simultaneous onset of Southern Hemisphere respiratory virus season (April 2026) with continued Northern Hemisphere transmission creates a year-round dual-hemisphere influenza pressure scenario
Co-occurrence of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika risk vectors creates compounded arboviral threat requiring integrated rather than disease-specific vector control
Measles and yellow fever alerts both issued in early 2026 indicate broader regional immunization program gaps potentially exacerbated by COVID-19 pandemic-era disruptions
PAHO GLP-1 medication misuse alert reflects an emerging non-communicable intersection with health system capacity that could divert resources from infectious disease response
